topic: DeepSeek's Claude Code rival is an MIT repo you run locally
title: DeepSeek's Claude Code Rival Is A Repo You Run
description: DeepSeek's Claude Code rival is not a hosted app: it is an MIT-licensed repo that runs on your own machine with the model endpoint of your choice. You'll learn what dsh-superagent actually is, what the router-worker split buys, and the catches. Subscribe for daily local AI shorts. (Narration is AI-generated.)
hook_text: It's a repo, and it's yours
hook_candidates: You think DeepSeek launched an app. It's a repo, and it's yours.
One npx command. DeepSeek's rival agent wakes up on localhost.

Five thousand three hundred stars for scaffolding without a brain.

Worth cloning tonight? Real agent scaffolding, rough and yours.
DeepSeek shipped a Claude Code rival with no model inside.
A router, spare sessions, one repo: DeepSeek's answer to attention.
DeepSeek's 'Super-Agent' watches one repo and answers with pull requests.
narration_full: You think DeepSeek launched an app. It's a repo, and it's yours. Bloomberg's own sentence calls it the new open-source offering. The thing itself is dsh-superagent, an MIT repo you run on your gaming PC. It's a profile of DeepSeek Harness, the scaffolding that lets a model call tools. No brain included: you pick the model provider, even your own self-hosted server. A Router talks to people; Workers each take one Ticket in its own directory. DeepSeek's reason: you can follow only three to five sessions. DeepSeek's fifteen point seven minute figure is a synthetic simulation, not a benchmark. The repo fences itself: research prototype, not a product, with danger-full-access to your user account. Worth cloning, not worth marrying.
